Updated read-through using the August 2022 Beige Book:

- Growth and demand: Beige Book points to flat-to-modest overall activity, with notable cooling in interest-sensitive sectors. Residential real estate weakened materially on higher mortgage rates; CRE softened. New York District reported increased recession risk even as tourism remained strong and employment continued to rise.
- Labor and prices: Labor markets stayed tight with ongoing job gains, but some input costs eased (reports of lower steel, lumber, and copper prices). Overall price pressures remained elevated, though goods-side disinflationary signs emerged alongside lower fuel prices.
- Credit conditions: Consistent with the July 2022 SLOOS, banks saw stronger demand in C&I and credit cards (likely precautionary/working-capital driven), while standards tightened across multiple categories. This procyclical tightening compounds the FOMC’s hawkish stance (75 bp hike to 3–3.25% and ongoing balance-sheet runoff).
- Net take: Beige Book corroborates tighter financial conditions and slowing in housing/CRE, but shows some offset from easing input costs and resilient services/tourism and employment. Compared with the SLOOS-only view, the Beige Book slightly tempers the downside by hinting at early price relief, though the growth outlook remains pressured.

Given these Beige Book insights, I’m nudging the prior -0.50 modestly less negative to reflect the mix of softer growth with tentative input-cost relief and still-firm labor/services.
